items.note: S1.3.1.1 gives the end result (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) with restored scratch on three-element subsets, but calls all three stages forward invocations, whereas stage 2 is the inverse schedule from Y to X (lines 731-732, 761-763). The per-invocation y_S <- y_S + x_S, the eight-row schedule and the net map (JV+RG)x are absent, so nothing is derived.

It has the mechanism: a common frame per gate commutes with pointwise linear gates and intermediate frames cancel. It writes the endpoint operator as D_sink D_source^{-1} 'on each role' and drops the routing w->rho(w) and the sign eps_w of eq. (817-822). A one-line infer step, not a derivation.

Nested nondegenerate labels in an m-dimensional bilinear space, with central-wire edges as the only decreasing edges, are stated, and L<N/2 appears in words in S1.3.1.4. Missing: the time 3->4 edge, the loss h, L=Ich, the budget Wm-2N+2L, the ratios 100/539 and 101/539, and F^{(x)3} with triple indicator vectors. No derivation is given.

The plan states s<Wm and that the endpoint matrices give the shear H<-H+D on every role, scratch included. It omits the projection assignment P_U and -P_{U_a}, the explicit identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m, and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b. Its reason ('less than half the source ranks the interface adds') matches the paper's deficit N-2L_b>0 only in words.

Correct in substance: one translation kernel aI+bX_v (or its inverse) per orthonormal residual vector, s calls in total, and C^{(x)} on every role including scratch. Missing: the phase frame C_U = H^{(x)m} diag(i^{q_U}) H^{(x)m} and the count s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c; it says only s<Wm. The weight-additivity proof is absent.

s<Wm, s/W<m^tau and tau=sigma=1-2^{-50} all appear, but separately. The deficits eta_b and eta_c, the bound eta>20*2^{-50}, log m<20 and the L/N ratios that produce tau are absent. The plan never shows how the strict saving fixes tau.

S1.1 matches the elementary-streams lemma. S1.2 drops the hypothesis that the offset is prepared in b^{O(1)} time from the controls (and the prime-modulus conditions), so the O(V) claim is stated unconditionally. There are no sub-steps.

It follows the paper's route: factor A=E_1 Pi E_2, apply triangular factors by controlled shifts, and replace each one of Pi by a three-update sequence with one interchange. The elimination proof of the factorization (1375-1392) is only stated, and the choice of a fixed odd prime q avoiding all denominators (1413-1423) is missing.

It follows the paper's proof: cyclic row split into W role streams, edge shears by recursive interchanges, H<-H+D on every role, the three-update interchange, then F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) and F_k=O(e^tau). Missing: the fixed-tape depth-first schedule (parking stack, O(V) per node, 1559-1615) that justifies the O(1) term, and the explicit V/W child volume and W^{k-1} row divisibility.

Base-m splitting into power-width pieces, row padding to a multiple of W^k, and binary-to-radix-q padding are given. The essential step that makes rows exist is missing: the top rho=O(log e) digits of both chunks are exchanged and joined into a row field (1652-1683).

The route is right: edge factor into kernels, s child calls on e/m axes with C^{(x)} on every role, then H_0^{(x)D}=b^D S_D C^{(x)D} S_D. Missing: the change of basis P_M that moves residual directions onto coordinate slots (eq. 1858-1862), the inverse-child identity (C^{-1})^{(x)f}=(-i)^f Z C Z, and the reduction of P_M to a fixed number of binary row additions.

It follows the proof: eight conditional rotations that restore w, packed cyclic shifts correct off the guard-failure set of fraction 80(f-1)2^{-K}, and repair by extraction and radix sort. Only the asymptotic O(V(L^tau+1)) is stated: the explicit bound with M A^3 and delta_bad M A(R+A), and the family conditions under which it simplifies, are missing.

The recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) is stated correctly with its reason (s calls on V/W streams). Missing: where the rows come from (the first q_0 chunks as a row index, 2306-2323), the leaf bound F(e)=O(e), the internal and leaf sums, and the condition max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}<lambda'.

The statement matches: O(V d^{lambda'}), error < sqrt2 2^{-p}, exact evaluation with one truncation, and Delta=o(p) from eps C_1<1. The proof route (depth bound, denominator and magnitude growth, row construction plus recurrence, conversion, disk preservation) is the paper's. The uniform packed-cost check (2696-2735) is only implicit.

Character cancellation, DIF with signed-shift twiddles, bit-reversed storage, round grouping and the three cost terms all follow the paper. The statement omits the error bound sqrt2 l 2^{-p} and the layout permutation L in the exact counterparts LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}.
Evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, the separation |h_j|<B_0/2, centered extraction, negacyclic reduction and truncation, and the four products costing O(rp log(rp)) all match the proof.

Two forward transforms in their common LB order, pointwise packed products, the opposite transform and the exact scale by M, with the stated error and cost. The commuting of the product with a common record permutation is given as the motivation.

The identity P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA, its tensor form, the errors and costs, and the O(Tp d^2(1+l^tau)) axis exposure are correct. The derivation names the Harvey-van der Hoeven identity and the Neumann inversion but not the construction of A=S/2 and B_0=D'J'C, or the normalizations whose product is 2^{-2alpha^2}.

Both identities are stated correctly, and S5.4 gives the paper's reason (F^+R=R^{-1}F^+, and permutations commute with pointwise products). The chirp array a is not defined and the Bluestein coefficient check is not shown, so this is counted as stated.
Sizes, the prime-interval count, T/2<S<T and alpha^4 theta_i>p follow the paper. The fixed list omits lambda=1-2^{-52}, beta and C_1, and eta=1/(4d) and alpha are never defined.
The isomorphism x -> prod x_i^{mu_i}, the triangular mixed-radix coordinates implemented by prefix-controlled shifts, and the O(Tp d^2(1+l^tau)) cost all match.
The twist x_d -> zeta y, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j, and M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g) are exactly the paper's.

The chirp transform, the source transform with exact counterpart 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A = R F_s, and the six algorithm steps are reproduced in order. The digit scaling 2^{-b-2} appears only as the norm bound 1/4.

E_s, the norm and error of z, E_w, the final bound below 1/2, rounding and carries match the paper. E_s is asserted without the ring-convolution (<5TL) and chirp (<8TL) error steps that produce it, and gamma<=b/4 is not mentioned in the final inequality.

Margins g_1..g_7, min g_i=2^{-181}=2kappa, the row-by-row justification, o(Tp) setup and exceptional streams, and O(n(log n)^{1-kappa}) with a schoolbook cutoff all follow the paper. One small looseness in S7.7 is listed under errors.
S8 matches the intro: the bound gives T_A(n)/(n lg n)->0 along all lengths, so no eventual lower bound c_A n lg n holds. The paper gives no further derivation.

errors.says: Three stages of forward invocations ... send (X_a,Y_a) to (-Y_a,X_a).
errors.paper: Stage 1 and stage 3 are forward invocations from X to Y; stage 2 runs the inverse forward schedule from Y to X, giving X <- X - Y. This middle stage produces the sign and the exchange: (x,y) -> (x,y+x) -> (-y,y+x) -> (-y,x).

errors.says: each edge's orthogonal residual has dimension equal to the number of smaller operations the edge needs.
errors.paper: In the bit network the N source edges of X_a have zero dimension change but edge matrix 2P_{U_a} of rank one. These are the stated exceptions that turn Wm-2N+2L into s_b=Wm-N+2L.

errors.says: only the endpoint operator D_sink D_source^{-1} acts on each role.
errors.paper: A route from input role w to output role rho(w) applies eps_w D_{sink(rho(w))} D_{source(w)}^{-1}. The sink is that of the routed role and carries the scalar sign, which matters for the bank exchange.

errors.says: Adding to a target field an offset computed from earlier control fields ... takes O(V) steps when the target field follows its controls.
errors.paper: The O(V) bound requires that the offset can be prepared in b^{O(1)} time from the fixed number of control values, with q prime and the coefficient conditions stated.
The bad-address fraction is O(d 2^{-K}) (80(f-1)2^{-K} in the lemma), and the sorting cost is O(V p^{A'} 2^{-K}).

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to the main bound: bit network, frames, labels, s<Wm, matrix shear, power-width recurrence, arbitrary-width interchange, then the complex network to the simultaneous layer, synthetic transforms, ring convolution, resampling and chirp, assembly, exact recovery and the cost table, with accurate quotes. It thins out at the source of the saving. The budget Wm-2N+2L, L=Ich, the L/N ratios, the projection matrices with the endpoint identity M_sink-M_source=I_m, and the derivation of tau=1-2^{-50} from the deficits are all missing, so s<Wm and s/W<m^tau are asserted rather than computed. The row constructions (high digits as rows in the arbitrary-width interchange, the first q_0 chunks in the layer) are also missing.

steps.note: The exchange (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) on three-element subsets with restored scratch is stated. h=100, N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3 are never given, and stage 2 is misdescribed as forward. Conservative verdict, since the defining quantities are absent.

A common invertible frame per gate commutes with the pointwise gate, intermediate frames cancel, and only the endpoint operator acts. The method says intermediate frames are chosen to make edge changes cheap. Routing and sign are dropped.

Nested nondegenerate labels in an m-dimensional bilinear space are stated, with central-wire edges as the only decreasing edges. The space F^{(x)3}, the time 3->4 edge and the loss of h per central wire are missing.

'Residual dimension equals the number of smaller operations' and 'source ranks that the rational interface adds' allude to it. There is no P_V-P_U, no rank = dim V - dim U, and no rank-one exception on the N source edges; the per-edge claim even overstates the equality.
Neither the budget Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich nor s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b appears; S1.3.1.4 only describes the rank sum in words.
S1.3.1.4 says in words that the dimension lost is less than half the added source ranks, hence s<Wm. The ratios 100/539 and 101/539 and the deficit N-2L>0 are not given.

S1.3.3a says the endpoint matrices give the shear H<-H+D on every role, scratch included, which is the identity's content and role. The explicit M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m and the -P_{U_a} source matrix are not written.
A=E_1 Pi E_2, exactly a interchanges plus O(V), and 'the number of recursive calls is the sum of the edge ranks' are all present.

F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), s/W<m^tau and F_k=O(e^tau) are present, and the V/W child volume is implicit in the motivation. tau=1-2^{-50} appears only as a fixed parameter: its derivation from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20 is absent.

central.summary: The plan reconstructs the frame mechanism, the endpoint shear, the rank-to-recursive-call conversion and the recurrence (C2, C7, C8, C9). The numerical core of the saving is only alluded to: the network's parameters h, N and m, the label losses of h on central edges, the rank-equals-dimension-change rule with its N source exceptions, the budget Wm-2N+2L, and the ratios L/N<1/2. So the plan asserts s<Wm rather than reconstructing why it holds.
